Take this free CTET Paper 1 Solids Around Us online test — 10 exam-pattern MCQs with instant scoring and a worked explanation for every answer. The Solids Around Us chapter is a dependable source of marks in the CTET Paper I (Classes I–V) Mathematics section — and it is one you can master quickly with the right practice. This guide explains what CTET solids around us actually tests, the facts and formulas worth memorising, the mistakes that quietly cost marks, and a free 10-question online test you can take right now to check where you stand.

Work through the quiz below first, read the explanation for anything you miss, then use the chapter-test e-book at the end for full, exam-style practice. That "test → review → practise" loop is how serious CTET candidates turn a weak topic into a strong one.

What Solids Around Us covers in CTET Paper I Maths

At the primary level this chapter blends content knowledge with pedagogy — how young children learn the idea. Expect questions on:

  • Cubes, cuboids, spheres, cylinders and cones
  • Faces, edges and vertices of each solid
  • Which solids roll and which slide
  • Real-life examples of each solid

Practise the full syllabus free on the CTET Paper I Mathematics course at vidaara.org, then test yourself here.

Key facts and formulas to remember

  • A cube and a cuboid each have 6 faces, 12 edges and 8 vertices.
  • A sphere has 1 curved surface and no edges or vertices.
  • A cone has 1 flat face, 1 curved surface and a single vertex (apex).
  • A cylinder has 2 flat circular faces and 1 curved surface.

Common mistakes to avoid

  • Mixing up faces, edges and vertices.
  • Thinking a cylinder has vertices (it has none).

quiz.title: CTET Solids Around Us Practice Quiz
quiz.intro: Ten CTET Paper I – pattern questions on Solids Around Us. Pick an answer for each, then press Check my score.
quiz.about: CTET Paper 1 Maths: Solids Around Us

questions.q: A child brings an object to school that has a curved surface but also has one flat circular face. It tapers to a point. The object can be:
questions.explanation: The sharpened part of a pencil tip has a flat circular base (where the wood meets the lead) and tapers to a point (the tip). This represents a cone. A glass tumbler is a cylinder, and an orange is a sphere.

questions.q: A teacher asks students to bring a solid that has only curved faces. Which of the following objects should a student bring?
questions.explanation: A cricket ball is a sphere. A sphere has only 1 face, and that face is entirely curved. It has no flat faces. A book and a chalk box are cuboids (flat faces only), and an ice cream cone has a curved face and a flat circular face.

questions.q: How many curved surfaces does a cube have?

questions.explanation: a cube has only flat faces, so it cannot roll (it slides).

questions.q: A child describes a solid by saying, 'It has no vertices.' Which of the following solids could the child be talking about?
questions.explanation: A vertex is a corner where edges meet. A sphere has a continuous curved surface with no edges; therefore, it has no vertices. A cube and cuboid have 8 vertices, while a cone has 1 vertex (the apex).

questions.q: Which of the following solids can both roll and slide?
questions.explanation: A cylinder can roll on its curved surface and slide on its flat circular faces. A sphere only rolls; a cuboid and cube only slide (they have no curved surfaces).

questions.q: The flat (circular) face of a cylinder is in the shape of a ___.
questions.explanation: The flat face of a cylinder is a circle.

questions.q: A student brings a matchbox to class for a geometry activity. The teacher asks her to identify its shape. It is a:
questions.explanation: A matchbox has rectangular faces; opposite sides are equal, but the length, width, and height are different. This makes it a cuboid.

questions.q: The flat faces of a cube are in the shape of a ___.
questions.explanation: Each flat face of a cube is a square.

questions.q: The number of edges in a sphere is:
questions.explanation: An edge is defined as the meeting point of two faces. A sphere has a single, continuous curved face with no boundaries; therefore, it has 0 edges.

faq.q: How many faces, edges and vertices does a cube have?
faq.a: A cube has 6 faces, 12 edges and 8 vertices.
Solids with a curved surface — the sphere, cylinder and cone — can roll. A cube and cuboid have only flat faces, so they slide.
